draft.title: Handling Media-Heavy and JavaScript-Only Sites in Offline HTML-to-Markdown with Local LLMs
draft.body: A mid-2025 project uses local LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B/8B with llama.cpp) to convert HTML pages to Markdown offline, aiming to outperform tools like Readability. The approach analyzes a page’s content type and structure using BeautifulSoup, then generates tailored extraction strategies with the LLM. While this works well on typical article or blog pages, it struggles with media-heavy or JavaScript-only sites without browser rendering. Given these limitations, what practical methods have others found to improve extraction quality for such complex sites in a fully offline environment? Is it feasible to enhance content capture without embedding a browser engine, or does offline processing inherently require some hybrid approach? Insights on balancing offline constraints with extraction fidelity would be helpful.
